chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yaqṭīn, he said:
I asked al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام about the deceased: is there the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer) in it, or not?

He said: Wash the deceased. Begin with his forearms, then wash them with al-ḥuruḍ, then his face and his head with lote leaves, then water is poured over him three times. And do not wash him except while in a shirt; a man inserts his hand and pours over him from above. And something of lote leaves and something of camphor are placed in the water. And he does not press his abdomen unless he fears something nearby, in which case he wipes it gently without pressing. Then the one who washed him washes his hand before shrouding him up to the shoulders three times; then when he has shrouded him, he performs ghusl (ritual bath).

So it does not contradict the earlier reports, because what the report contains is an explanation of the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, and it did not require an explanation of the details of wudu (ablution), because that is known. And it did not refrain from explaining it because it is not obligatory; rather, because of what we have stated before. As for what has been narrated in reports that the ghusl of the deceased is like the ghusl of the junub alike, then if the ghusl of janabah does not contain wudu, then likewise the ghusl of the deceased; this is opposed by the reports which were narrated stating that every ghusl contains wudu except ghusl from janabah. And if the ghusl of the deceased is other than the ghusl of janabah, then wudu must be established in it. Moreover, the intent in their saying, 'the ghusl of the deceased is like the ghusl of janabah,' is the explanation of the manner of ghusl and observing the sequence in it, because the two are of one pattern, even if one of them contains wudu and the other does not, just as the ghusl of menstruation is like the ghusl of janabah, even though it contains wudu according to what we have explained, while the ghusl of janabah does not.

key_terms.السِّدْرِ: lote leaves used in the washing water
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity used here for comparison of ghusl rulings
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person being prepared and washed
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: ritual ablution discussed as a legal component of certain forms of ghusl
key_terms.غَسِّلِ: wash; the command to perform the ritual washing
key_terms.كَافُورٍ: camphor added to the water for washing the deceased
key_terms.وُضُوءُ الصَّلَاةِ: the ablution of salat (prayer), discussed here as part of funeral washing

ai.seo_question: Is wudu required before the ghusl of the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the procedure for washing the deceased and addresses whether wudu (ablution) is included before the ghusl (ritual bath) of the dead. It also reconciles narrations by explaining that the likeness between the ghusl of the deceased and the ghusl of janabah concerns the method and order of washing, not necessarily the ruling regarding wudu.
